messages:
chris: Quick sync — should clients see a 503 when a route is degraded to fallback? thinking about UX + SLOs for hosted customers :thinking:

maya: IMO no, 503 is 'down' — degraded/fallback is still a valid response. prefer 200 with explicit header + telemetry flag.

chris: so header-based signal + stable HTTP code. curious about SDK ergonomics — we want something client-friendly and not too noisy.

linh: +1 to headers. propose: X-Redwood-Route-State: degraded | normal | fallback, and X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: quota|capacity|model-quality. SDK can surface both.

felix: what about transient infra: capacity shortages vs model quality regressions are different. For capacity we should surface 503/429 depending on quota vs overloaded. For quality fallback (e.g., small-quantized model) return 200 but mark degraded.

maya: agree. mapping idea: 
- 429 -> client exceeded quota (explicit)
- 503 -> node/operator-level outage or routed-to-down region
- 200 + X-Redwood-Route-State: degraded -> graceful fallback (lower perf/quality)

chris: that mapping seems reasonable. two followups: console UX + telemetry gates. we need clear signals in dashboards and runbooks.

linh: telemetry proposal: emit metrics: route.state{normal,degraded,failed}, route.fallback_reason{quota,capacity,quality}, tenant.quota_hits, client.visible_status. Also tag model_variant and sequence_len_bucket.

maya: console should show per-route % degraded over 1h/24h, and flag when degraded ratio > 5% for a canary or >1% for prod routes. link to eval prompt sets so teams can see quality diffs.

felix: on rollout UX: when we roll a model variant that increases degraded count, we should auto-create an alert and a canary task in the console with sample prompts + diff. don't want silent regressions.

chris: +1. also need clear client copy for SDKs and docs. suggestion: 429 body includes retry_after + console_url. 200-degraded includes a lightweight hint object: 
```json
{
  "redwood": {
    "route_state": "degraded",
    "fallback_reason": "quota",
    "hint": "use dedicated or increase quota"
  }
}
```

linh: that JSON snippet is fine but keep it opt-in — some clients want minimal payload. make header primary signal and hint object optional when Accept: application/redwood+json.

maya: also add a short human-friendly message for quick debugging: X-Redwood-Client-Message: "request served by fallback model; quality may be reduced". small and parseable.

felix: question: do we want SDKs to automatically retry on degraded->normal transition? risky if quality matters. maybe SDK exposes is_degraded boolean and leaves retry to app.

chris: agreed — do not auto-retry. expose info and a helper to surface a banner in UI.

ops-bot: deploy:runtime-config v2 -> route-state-headers rolled out to 10% of nodes (canary) :rocket:

maya: canary is good. please ensure we emit route.state metrics at debug level during canary so we can tune thresholds without alert storms.

linh: action items:
- frontend/SDK: add header parsing + optional hint object (linh, PR)
- telemetry: add route.state + fallback_reason metrics + model_variant tag (felix, infra-metrics)
- console: show degraded % and link to eval diffs (maya, console)
- product: write client docs/copy for 429/503/200-degraded mapping (chris)

chris: i'll draft the client phrases and runbook blurb, pinging for review. tagging for follow-up: @maya @linh @felix.

maya: lgtm. small nit — make sure quota 429 includes "quota_remaining": 0 in body so clients can backoff gracefully.

felix: also recommend a discrete telemetry flag 'client_visible_status' that mirrors header for easier filtering (since logs lost headers sometimes).

chris: noted. thanks everyone — we'll iterate on exact header names in the RFC but agree on the high-level mapping and console gating. :thumbsup:
